title: Ambiguity fallthrough triage — personal heuristics and quick examples
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal cheat-sheet for handling 'fallthrough' ambiguous labeling cases I keep hitting in sample audits. Not final — mostly notes-to-self + example bank for pair adjudication and small automation heuristics.

How I use this:
- When a labeler marks "ABSTAIN" or picks multiple conflicting spans, run through these quick checks before escalating.
- Keep rulings conservative: prefer recall-preserving abstain when downstream consumer unknown.

Core heuristics (prioritized):
1) Schema first: ensure candidate span actually maps to a supported label type. If not, mark NON-ENTITY.
2) Context window: expand to sentence-level before deciding. Short spans that look like fragments often resolve with nearby tokens.
3) Prefer canonicalization: if span looks like a brand variant (e.g., "Acme corp.", "Acme"), map to single canonical label if canonical exists in knowledge list.
4) Longest-descriptive-span: when multiple overlapping spans, choose the span that contains descriptive qualifiers (dates, modifiers) unless instruction explicitly says "shortest".
5) Numeric ambiguity: numbers with units -> preserve unit token. Standalone digits -> check provenance (order id vs quantity).
6) Email/URL heuristics: if token has @ or domain-like suffix, treat as CONTACT/URL even if malformed (heuristic flag for noisy OCR).

Edge-case checklist (triage flow):
- OCR-induced hyphenation: try merge-with-neighbor if hyphen at line break (e.g., "micro-
batch" -> "microbatch"). If unsure, leave annotation span to include both tokens.
- Parenthetical qualifiers: "Company (holding)" -> label full phrase if parenthetical adds meaning; otherwise label head token only.
- Slash-separated terms: prefer split labels if both are valid entities ("sugar/flour" -> two items), otherwise single span if phrase behaves as unit ("GM/Toyota alliance").
- Date fragments: "Q1 2024" -> single DATE; "2024-" -> mark as PARTIAL_DATE and flag for human fix.
- Currency + rounding: "$5k" -> normalize to USD and note magnitude (keep literal span in text).

Small adjudication examples (explicit decisions):
1) Text: "met with Acme corp., Uber, and Lyft last week"
   - Preferred: label "Acme corp." as ORG (canonical: ACME_CORP), "Uber" ORG, "Lyft" ORG.
   - Rationale: plain list, capitalization consistent. If lowercased in raw OCR, check lexicon before abstain.

2) Text: "order # 12345/12346"
   - Preferred: two ORDER_ID spans (split on slash) if both patterns match ticket format. If ambiguous -> single span and tag as ORDER_ID_MULTI.

3) Text: "I give my consent (see: privacy redwood.example.com)"
   - Preferred: label URL span even without http://; label "privacy" as neither.

4) Text: "the patient was given 50mg aspirin"
   - Preferred: "50mg" -> DOSAGE, "aspirin" -> DRUG, ensure tokenization keeps numeric unit attached.

Ambiguity examples I've seen repeatedly (with quick rule):
- Short surnames vs common nouns: "Cook" -> if preceded by title ("Chef Cook", "Mr. Cook") -> PERSON else check frequency list; if frequent-noun context ("to cook dinner") -> NON-ENTITY.
- Abbreviations with periods: "U.S." -> COUNTRY when context international; else check for acronym list.
- Hyphenated locations: "New York-based" -> label "New York" as LOCATION, avoid including the hyphen unless explicit region token needed.

Heuristic flags for automation (small script ideas):
- Flag low-confidence numeric spans where leading/trailing punctuation mismatches pattern (e.g., trailing comma inside digits).
- Auto-merge hyphen-break neighbors when both tokens individually match entity patterns > 0.9 confidence.
- Auto-suggest canonical ORG names from lexicon and show diff to labeler (fast accept).

Adjudication quick protocol (pair review):
- Round 1: try heuristics above (2–3 minutes per example).
- Round 2: if still contested, check linked artifacts (LINEAR ticket / spec). If no spec, prefer CONSERVATIVE (abstain or NON-ENTITY) and add note.
- Add short rationale tag on adjudicated span: e.g., "adjudicated:merged-hyphen" or "adjudicated:canonicalized".

Notes from recent sample audit (Feb 2025):
- ~18% of conflicts were OCR line-break hyphenation (microbatch & merge rule would fix ~70% of these).
- Frequent false positives: short uppercase acronyms in all-caps text -> many are section headers, not entities.
- Suggest adding simple header-detection prefilter: if short token sequence all caps and surrounding tokens are newline markers, suppress labeling.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Where do we land on partial dates? full DATE vs PARTIAL_DATE tag — need spec for downstream consumer. (action: ping analytics)
- Should we auto-split slash IDs by default? Edge case: some product codes intentionally contain slashes. (action: sample 200 slash cases)
- Create small evaluation: run hyphen-merge heuristic on 5k samples and measure conflict reduction. (action: Lucas to run script)

Quick commands / helpers (notes-to-self):
- grep patterns: "\b\n- raise LINEAR-4872 for new canonical mapping additions"
- add lexicon lookup to labeler UI (low-effort win)

Random pinboard (tiny ideas to try later):
- UI: show 'likely merge' suggestion when adjacent tokens both entity-like and hyphen slash punctuation between them.
- Label export: include "adjudication_reason" field so model fine-tuning can learn our fallthrough patterns.

If anything above should be formalized, capture as tiny Confluence stub and assign to "annotation-team". For now this is personal reference for pair adjudication and quick triage.

——
Last quick thought: when in doubt and no downstream consumer spec, prefer recall-preserving abstain + short note. Keeps training set safer than over-labeling noisy positives.

End of file.
